headline: Apple is catching up with Siri with new Apple Watch features, as agentic AI expectations shift
summary: Expectations surrounding agentic assistants are quickly shifting. But two Apple Watch features show Apple will not watch from the sidelines yet again.
details: Apple is reportedly enhancing Siri's capabilities, particularly with new features for the Apple Watch. This move signals Apple's intent to remain competitive in the rapidly evolving landscape of AI-powered assistants.

The tech industry is seeing a swift shift in expectations for "agentic assistants," which can perform complex tasks autonomously. Apple's efforts aim to bring Siri closer to these advanced capabilities.
These developments suggest Apple is actively working to prevent Siri from falling further behind rivals, ensuring its virtual assistant can meet future user demands.

headline_marked: Moderna and Merck say their [[mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42%]]
headline: Moderna and Merck say their mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42%
summary: A personalized mRNA vaccine against melanoma, developed by Merck and Moderna, reduced the risk of death or recurrence by 42% in a late-stage trial. This significant advance has prompted engagement with regulatory authorities.
details: Personalized mRNA vaccines for melanoma, the deadliest form of skin cancer, reduced the risk of death or recurrence by 42% compared to standard treatment in a late-stage trial. Pharmaceutical partners Merck and Moderna announced these top-line results.

The companies are now engaging with regulatory authorities to get the vaccine approved. This success significantly bolsters hope that mRNA vaccines and individualized cancer-targeting medicines can offer a new paradigm for cancer therapies.

Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel stated that the trial results mark a defining moment for their vision of developing cancer treatments uniquely matched to each patient’s tumor. He emphasized that mRNA has the potential to fundamentally change how cancer is treated.

The Phase 3 trial included 1,137 patients with stage IIB–IV melanoma that had been surgically removed. Patients were randomized to receive either a combination treatment of the personalized mRNA vaccine with Merck’s Keytruda, or Keytruda alone.

The tailored mRNA vaccine, intismeran (mRNA-4157), uses synthetic mRNA to hold unique genetic coding for up to 34 mutations in a patient's own cancer cells. Researchers compare genetic sequences to identify cancer-specific mutations that can help the immune system target only cancer cells.

After two years, 82% of participants receiving the intismeran-Keytruda treatment were still alive without recurrence, compared to 70% in the Keytruda-placebo group. This demonstrates the 42% reduction in the risk of recurrence or death.

For distant metastasis-free survival, the intismeran-Keytruda treatment reduced the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38%. At the trial's end, 88.5% of the combination group were alive without distant metastasis, versus 80% in the control group.

While the treatment effect was slightly less potent than a five-year Phase 2 trial, this Phase 3 study is the first to show a clinically meaningful improvement over standard-of-care KEYTRUDA in patients with resected melanoma. This sets a new benchmark in adjuvant treatment.
